# checkpoint-axi

Inspect Check Point Email Security through compact, guarded AXI commands.
Start investigations with the compact [agent guide](../../docs/agent-guide.md), which includes the read allowlist, bounded one-call forms and failure recovery.
See [README's introduction](../../README.md#checkpoint-axi) for shipped capabilities and [write guidance](../../docs/writes.md#email-writes) before requesting mutations.
Use `npx -y @knowttl/checkpoint-axi` without a global install.
Bare `--version`, `-v` and `-V` print the package version.

Run npx -y @knowttl/checkpoint-axi config path; configure a region, clientId and clientSecret env/file SecretRef.
Secrets use environment/file SecretRefs, never inline values, argv or chat.
Regions are us, eu, ca, au, uk, uae and in; arbitrary origins are refused.

```sh
npx -y @knowttl/checkpoint-axi
npx -y @knowttl/checkpoint-axi home --profile example
npx -y @knowttl/checkpoint-axi auth status
npx -y @knowttl/checkpoint-axi doctor
npx -y @knowttl/checkpoint-axi email search
npx -y @knowttl/checkpoint-axi email show <id>
```

Home and the optional checkpoint-axi-hook binary read local context only.
Configure a session hook only on explicit request; it is never installed automatically.
Use the hook for ambient discovery or this skill for on-demand discovery.
Local auth status validates secret availability and file security without authenticating to the API.
Do not infer API access from a local pass.
Doctor explicitly authenticates and checks one email search page over the past 24 hours.
It reports region, SaaS and pass/fail per check without tenant data; a failed check exits 1.
Use --saas to override the profile SaaS for doctor, email search or event list; the default is office365_emails.
AUTH_SHAPE_UNVERIFIED requires commissioning of the undocumented token response shape (guide page 8).
Tokens stay in memory; verified TLS and the fixed region map are mandatory.
Read sessions allow at most 10 HTTP requests; write sessions allow at most 44.
Both are bounded by 8 MiB of JSON and 60 seconds including auth and read retries; binary downloads have a separate 50 MiB cap per response.
Email search defaults to 50 compact rows and a 24-hour window; --start-date and --end-date require ISO timestamps with timezones and a positive window of at most 31 days (guide pages 18-27).
Use --limit <1-1000> or --all, which caps output at 1000 rows within the shared transport budget.
Use --saas-entity for an entity type or --filter for a JSON array of {saasAttrName, saasAttrOp, saasAttrValue} filters (guide pages 19-20).
saasAttrName is a field path, not a closed enum (guide pages 19-20).
Documented examples: entityPayload.subject, entityPayload.fromEmail, entityPayload.attachmentCount.
Other documented email payload paths (pages 15-16, 24-25): entityPayload.internetMessageId, entityPayload.received, entityPayload.size, entityPayload.emailLinks, entityPayload.attachments, entityPayload.mode, entityPayload.recipients, entityPayload.fromDomain, entityPayload.fromUser, entityPayload.fromName, entityPayload.to, entityPayload.toUser, entityPayload.cc, entityPayload.ccUser, entityPayload.bcc, entityPayload.bccUser, entityPayload.replyToEmail, entityPayload.replyToNickname, entityPayload.isRead, entityPayload.isDeleted, entityPayload.isIncoming, entityPayload.isInternal, entityPayload.isOutgoing, entityPayload.isQuarantined, entityPayload.isQuarantineNotification, entityPayload.isRestored, entityPayload.isRestoreRequested, entityPayload.isRestoreDeclined, entityPayload.saasSpamVerdict, entityPayload.SpfResult.
saasAttrOp: is, contains, startsWith, isEmpty, isNot, notContains, isNotEmpty, greaterThan, lessThan.
The guide defines operators globally, without a per-field compatibility matrix; examples pair fromEmail with is and attachmentCount with greaterThan.
saasAttrValue is a string.
See [email-read guidance](../../docs/reads.md#email-reads) for continuation, completion status, cursor safety and page replay limitations.
Email show <id> includes payload, verdicts, actions taken and available actions (guide pages 10-18).
Email search and event list accept --expand for read-only show details in each successful row's detail field.
Expansion is off by default; --expand-limit caps detail attempts (default 5, range 1-8), and --expand-requests caps total HTTP requests (default 10, range 2-10), including auth, list pages and retries.
Both limit flags require --expand; listing runs first and shares the 60-second and 8 MiB transport budgets with detail reads.
Inspect the expansion object's expanded, complete and notExpanded fields for every unexpanded ID and its reason: item-cap-reached, request-cap-reached, budget-exhausted or per-item-error (with an error code).
Partial expansion keeps every list row and successful detail; list complete/cursor describe pagination separately.
Use --fields emails,expansion or --fields events,expansion to retain expansion status; --full restores full strings after redaction.
With --all, list pages can consume the entire request budget before any detail is expanded; reduce the list limit or use individual show reads for remaining IDs.
Expansion never downloads files, invokes available actions or changes remote state.
Use --full for strings truncated at 500 characters and --fields for top-level output projection.
Cursor strings are never truncated; secret-derived strings are redacted before previews.
Downloads require file-profile downloads.allow and an absolute new --out file, created exclusively with mode 0600 or a protected Windows DACL.
Use email download <entity-id> [--original], attachment download <entity-id> <attachment-id> or attachment download-all <entity-id>, always with --out /absolute/new-file.
Downloads buffer at most 50 MiB per response, require a valid matching x-av-sha256 and sync verified bytes to disk; failures remove the new output.
Only path, size and sha256 are printed; binary content never enters stdout and server filenames are ignored.
Email requires profile scope as the scopes header; attachments take optional --scope query overriding profile scope.
Scope authorization remains unverified, as does email/ZIP hash availability because the guide only documents x-av-sha256 for individual attachments (pages 131-137).
The mandatory hash policy fails closed on missing headers; verify manually before assuming live download support.
ZIP HTTP 200 may contain only some attachments; archives are never automatically extracted.
See [download guidance](../../docs/downloads.md) for retry limits, output safety and commissioning limitations.
Event action --ids <ids> --name <action> previews by default and requires the exact profile operation event.action.<name>, --execute and the preview's exact --confirm to send once.
Every target must offer the action on both reads; nonempty actionParameter objects or repeated action names refuse ENDPOINT_UNVERIFIED until live commissioning resolves the object/string contradiction (guide pages 36-37, 43).
Use event show <id> to inspect all available actions, including deferred parameterized actions.
Accepted actions return task IDs; use task show <taskId> to inspect asynchronous execution without replaying ambiguous outcomes.
Event list supports documented selectors and shares email search bounds and continuation; event show preserves actions and task show reads asynchronous status (guide pages 30-42).
Task show reads once by default; use task show <id> --wait --timeout 30 for bounded read-only polling.
--timeout is required with --wait (integer seconds, range 1-60); --poll-interval defaults to 2 seconds (range 1-10), and --wait-requests defaults to 10 total HTTP requests (range 2-10), including auth and retries.
Wait stops on completed, failed or stopped; init, inprogress and paused remain non-terminal.
The task snapshot contains the final status; wait reports terminal, polls (validated status snapshots) and reason (terminal, timeout or budget).
A non-terminal stop exits 0 with the last snapshot and a read-only next-step hint; inspect wait even on exit 0 and include task,wait,help with --fields.
Timeout covers auth, requests, retries and delays within the shared 8 MiB response cap; failures before any snapshot remain errors.
Waiting never resubmits an action or changes remote state; a failed or stopped task is terminal, not successful execution.
Exception list/show accept phishing-allow, phishing-block, spam-allow, anomaly, click-time, malware, url and dlp (guide pages 49-123).
For malware, url and dlp, --type is required; run exception list --help for the documented values.
Click-time --items selects item routes; by default list routes are used.
Exception show takes an ID or value as a positional argument after the kind; values are encoded as one path segment.
Anomaly show refuses with ENDPOINT_UNVERIFIED because no detail endpoint or response identity is documented (pages 83-84).
Exception lists default to 50 rows; --limit or --all bounds results at 1000 rows within transport budgets.
No exception continuation request parameter is documented; incomplete results report complete: false without inventing scroll requests.
Anti-Phishing requests are spaced at 1 request/second; other exception requests at 10 requests/second, including read retries.
Undocumented exception response shapes are preserved as JSON values and marked responseSchema: unverified; live behavior remains uncommissioned.
For exception create/update/remove on phishing-allow, phishing-block and spam-allow, follow [Anti-Phishing and Spam write guidance](../../docs/writes.md#anti-phishing-and-spam-writes) for private input, replacement semantics, scope, confirmation and preflight/no-op behavior.
For anomaly create/remove and click-time create/update/remove/remove-items, follow [anomaly and click-time write guidance](../../docs/writes.md#anomaly-and-click-time-writes) for documented inputs, exact scope and confirmation, unverified target/response contracts and read-only reconciliation.
That guidance also owns the approved clear and collection-PUT commissioning deferrals; do not infer existence, identities or no-op state from undocumented JSON or replay a mutation to retrieve truncated output.
For malware/URL/DLP create, create-specific and update, follow [malware, URL and DLP write guidance](../../docs/writes.md#malware-url-and-dlp-writes) for private inputs, payload confirmation and unverified responses.
The six malware/URL/DLP remove/clear commands refuse ENDPOINT_UNVERIFIED before configuration or authentication; the guide duplicates create/delete requests, so live commissioning must establish their actual contracts.
All live-only facts remain unverified, including token response shape and lifetime, delete requests and download scopes.

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `npx -y @knowttl/checkpoint-axi attachment download` | Download one attachment to a new private file with profile opt-in, a 50 MiB cap and verified x-av-sha256; scope behavior is unverified (guide pages 133-135) |
| `npx -y @knowttl/checkpoint-axi attachment download-all` | Download available attachments as a ZIP to a new private file with opt-in, a 50 MiB cap and mandatory SHA-256 verification; ZIP hash availability and scopes are unverified; HTTP 200 may contain only some attachments (guide pages 135-137) |
| `npx -y @knowttl/checkpoint-axi auth status` | Validate the selected local profile and secret source without API calls |
| `npx -y @knowttl/checkpoint-axi config path` | Show config and state paths without reading files; --profile does not affect paths |
| `npx -y @knowttl/checkpoint-axi doctor` | Check regional API authentication and one bounded email search without printing tenant data |
| `npx -y @knowttl/checkpoint-axi email download` | Download an email to a new private file with profile opt-in, a 50 MiB cap and mandatory SHA-256 verification; scopes and email hash availability are unverified (guide pages 131-132) |
| `npx -y @knowttl/checkpoint-axi email quarantine` | Preview or request asynchronous email quarantine through the gated write coordinator (guide pages 28-30) |
| `npx -y @knowttl/checkpoint-axi email restore` | Preview or request asynchronous email restore through the gated write coordinator (guide pages 28-30) |
| `npx -y @knowttl/checkpoint-axi email search` | Search emails with a bounded date window and scroll continuation (API guide pages 18-27) |
| `npx -y @knowttl/checkpoint-axi email show` | Show one email with verdicts, actions and available actions (API guide pages 10-18) |
| `npx -y @knowttl/checkpoint-axi event action` | Preview or request a name-only event action; parameterized actions refuse ENDPOINT_UNVERIFIED pending commissioning (guide pages 35-37, 42-45) |
| `npx -y @knowttl/checkpoint-axi event list` | List security events with bounded scroll continuation (API guide pages 37-42) |
| `npx -y @knowttl/checkpoint-axi event show` | Show one event, actions taken and available actions (API guide pages 34-37) |
| `npx -y @knowttl/checkpoint-axi exception clear` | Refuse click-time/malware/url/dlp clear with ENDPOINT_UNVERIFIED until commissioning establishes counts and delete contracts (guide pages 87-88, 96-97, 107-110, 117-120, 128-131) |
| `npx -y @knowttl/checkpoint-axi exception create` | Preview or create one exception of any kind; anomaly/click-time/malware/url/dlp response identities are unverified (guide pages 61-64, 75-78, 84-85, 91-93, 102-105, 113-116, 123-126) |
| `npx -y @knowttl/checkpoint-axi exception list` | List bounded exceptions for phishing-allow, phishing-block, spam-allow, anomaly, click-time, malware, url or dlp (guide pages 49-123) |
| `npx -y @knowttl/checkpoint-axi exception remove` | Preview or remove one phishing/spam/anomaly/click-time exception by ID; malware/url/dlp refuse ENDPOINT_UNVERIFIED before authentication (guide pages 67-69, 81-82, 85-87, 98-99, 108-110, 119-120, 129-131) |
| `npx -y @knowttl/checkpoint-axi exception remove-items` | Preview or remove 1-20 click-time items by caller-supplied IDs; existence is unverified (guide pages 97-98) |
| `npx -y @knowttl/checkpoint-axi exception show` | Show an exception by kind and ID/value; anomaly refuses ENDPOINT_UNVERIFIED pending commissioning (guide pages 52-123) |
| `npx -y @knowttl/checkpoint-axi exception update` | Preview or replace one exception; phishing/spam/click-time require an ID; malware/url/dlp identify it in --input without an ID; anomaly unsupported (guide pages 64-67, 78-81, 94-96, 105-107, 116-117, 126-127) |
| `npx -y @knowttl/checkpoint-axi home` | Show local profile context without resolving secrets or making API calls |
| `npx -y @knowttl/checkpoint-axi profile list` | List file profiles without resolving secrets; --profile does not filter this list |
| `npx -y @knowttl/checkpoint-axi task show` | Show asynchronous task status and per-action details, optionally waiting within explicit bounds (API guide pages 30-33) |
